summary: A class-action lawsuit alleged Google Photos' face grouping feature scanned people's faces without the written notice and consent required by Illinois biometric law. Google agreed to a 100 million dollar settlement without admitting wrongdoing.
technical_summary: Google Photos' face grouping tool automatically identifies and clusters faces in uploaded photos and videos, creating face geometry data. Plaintiffs alleged it was done without notice, informed written consent or a published retention policy, as Illinois BIPA requires. Google later added opt-in consent.

summary: Research found Facebook's ad delivery system showed job and housing ads to different groups by gender and race even when advertisers targeted everyone. A later audit found job ads still skewed by gender.
technical_summary: Facebook's ad delivery optimization predicts which users will find ads relevant and optimizes for budget and engagement, producing demographic skew in who sees employment and housing ads despite neutral targeting. Audits using paired job ads showed skew not explained by qualifications. The platform does not disclose how delivery works.

summary: Researchers showed that widely used word embeddings trained on Google News text encode gender stereotypes, such as linking certain jobs more strongly with women or men. They proposed a method to reduce the bias.
technical_summary: Word embeddings used as input in many NLP systems, here trained on Google News, capture gender direction and stereotyped associations in their vector geometry. The study quantified direct and indirect bias and proposed algorithms that remove stereotypes while keeping useful properties. It was a research demonstration, not a deployed harm.

notes: Research finding about potential bias; no specific realized harm is described.

summary: A study found Google image search results under-represented women for some jobs, such as CEO. In 2015 the first woman shown for a CEO search was a Barbie doll, several rows down.
technical_summary: Google's image search ranking returned results whose gender mix for some occupations differed from real-world data, for instance 11 percent women for CEO versus 27 percent in US labor statistics. The ranking reflects patterns in web content and user behavior. Researchers found the skew can shift people's perceptions of who holds those jobs.

summary: Economists found the IRS audited Black taxpayers at roughly three to five times the rate of other taxpayers. The disparity appears to come from the algorithms that select returns for audit, not from individual agents.
technical_summary: IRS automated audit-selection algorithms, designed under budget constraints, disproportionately flag returns with easy-to-detect errors, such as certain credit claims, and avoid costlier business-income audits. Because filing patterns differ by group, race-blind selection produced large racial disparities. The algorithms are not publicly disclosed.

summary: A class-action lawsuit alleged Facebook's Tag Suggestions feature scanned users' faces and stored biometric data without consent, violating Illinois law. Facebook agreed to pay 550 million dollars to settle.

summary: Cruise driverless cars in San Francisco repeatedly stopped in the road and blocked traffic. On one night nearly 60 vehicles were disabled after losing contact with a Cruise server, and staff had to move cars manually.

summary: Chicago prosecutors charged a man with murder using ShotSpotter gunshot-detection audio. Reporting says an analyst had changed the system's initial classification of the sound from a firework to a gunshot. He spent nearly a year in jail before the case was dismissed.
technical_summary: ShotSpotter sensors flagged a loud sound, and its algorithm first classified it as a firework at a location about a mile from the alleged shooting. An analyst manually reclassified it as a gunshot and the company later issued a revised forensic report used as key evidence. The man was jailed until prosecutors dropped the case.

summary: Fourth-graders in China showed that a facial-recognition parcel locker could be opened with just a printed photo of the intended recipient. The company suspended the feature, which it said was in beta.
technical_summary: Hive Box smart lockers used camera-based face matching to release parcels without liveness detection, so a printed photo of the recipient's face was accepted. A TV host replicated the finding with a near-perfect success rate. The company suspended the beta feature after the report.

summary: An Italian court ruled that Deliveroo's rider-ranking algorithm discriminated against couriers. It lowered riders' reliability scores for late shift cancellations without considering reasons like illness, reducing their future work. Deliveroo said it no longer used that system.
technical_summary: Deliveroo's shift-booking system ranked riders by a 'reliability index' and offered busier time slots to higher-ranked riders. Cancelling a booked shift within 24 hours lowered the index regardless of legitimate reasons such as illness or strike, so affected riders received fewer opportunities. A Bologna court found this indirectly discriminatory.
